authority.header: include/openssl/x509v3.h.in:45-61 (the X509V3_EXT_* callback typedefs and the method struct)
authority.note: The authority decodes the extension octet string through ASN1_ITEM_ptr(method->it) and calls the first of i2s/i2v/i2r that is set. It does not check out, ext, the item or the decoded value. The candidate refuses a NULL out/ext, a NULL item and a NULL decode; those are recorded safety divergences (B49-R5, B49-R6, B49-R7), not authority behaviour.

chosen_family.why: The i2s arm is the first slot X509V3_EXT_print tries, before i2v and i2r, so the 11 i2s definitions share the same dispatcher path as the 22 B49 printers. The only production reader of an i2s slot is src/x509/v3_prn.rs:323-332, whose value is called at :346; a grep of `(*method).i2s` finds no other production read. The only other read is the test at src/x509/v3_ia5.rs:226 against a static row.

shared_contract: i2s slot contract stated on X509V3ExtMethod (src/x509/v3_lib.rs). X509V3_EXT_print resolves the row (src/x509/v3_prn.rs:283) under the registry read hold (:271-273), decodes through the row's own item (:308) and refuses a NULL decode (:317-320), then reads the i2s slot (:323-332) and calls it at :346. The non-NULL result is adopted as Option<OwnedStr> (:346) and released once at :374; the decoded value is released with the same item (:374-381). `ext_str` is exclusively the dispatcher's from decode to release: the callback must not free, retain or replace it. `method` is the live row, passed to the callback; the callback must not retain it. The callback may retain nothing and transfers ownership of its result.

entry_points: X509V3_EXT_print itself (src/x509/v3_prn.rs:254), the exported C ABI entry point, called directly by external consumers and by src/x509/t_acert.rs:429 and src/x509/t_req.rs:389.
X509V3_extensions_print (src/x509/v3_prn.rs:390) loops over a stack and calls X509V3_EXT_print at :447; reached from src/x509/t_x509.rs, src/x509/t_crl.rs and src/ocsp/ocsp_prn.rs.
X509V3_EXT_print_fp (src/x509/v3_prn.rs:470) wraps a FILE* in a BIO and calls X509V3_EXT_print at :483.
dispatch_paths.lookup: X509V3_EXT_get(ext) at src/x509/v3_prn.rs:283 -> X509V3_EXT_get_nid (standard_exts[] binary search, then the dynamic ext_list), all under the registry read hold.
dispatch_paths.decode: the row item is resolved once (ext_method_item, :296); None means the old-style d2i/ext_free pair, Err means a NULL item accessor and the failed-decode path.
dispatch_paths.slot: the first set of i2s/i2v/i2r wins (:323-369); the i2s call is f(method, ext_str) at :346, before i2v (:355) and i2r (:364).
dispatch_paths.result: the i2s result is adopted as Option<OwnedStr> at :346; NULL means the print fails (:350-351), non-NULL is printed at :349 and released by Drop at :374.
dispatch_paths.free: ASN1_item_free(ext_str, item) at :378 with the same item the decode used, or method->ext_free (:379-381).
dispatch_paths.lifetime: `method` must be live from the lookup through the callback; `ext_str` is exclusively this frame's from decode to :374-381 and is live across the callback. Neither is retained by the callback.
dispatch_paths.allocator: no allocator is involved in the dispatch itself: ext_str comes from the ASN.1 decoder on the CRYPTO_* seam; the i2s result is the callback's own seam block and is released with OPENSSL_free at v3_prn.c:130; the registry lock is one CRYPTO_RWLOCK allocated on first use (B49-R11).
dispatch_paths.second_reader: The only other i2s slot read is the unit test at src/x509/v3_ia5.rs:226 on a process-lifetime static row; it neither registers nor releases a dynamic row and does not need the hold.
dispatch_paths.arguments: i2s receives (method, ext_str) only. `ext` (the X509_EXTENSION) is the caller's; X509V3_EXT_print uses it before the slot to read the value (:276-279) and resolve the row (:283), and does not pass it to the callback. `out` (the BIO) is not passed to i2s at all. `method` is the live row and `ext_str` is the dispatcher-owned decoded value.
dispatch_paths.ctx: none: the i2s typedef has no X509V3_CTX parameter; X509V3_CTX is an s2i input, not an i2s input.
dispatch_paths.retention: the callback may retain nothing: not `method`, not `ext_str`, and not the extension or output BIO. Its non-NULL result transfers to the dispatcher, which owns it from :346 to :374.

row_liveness.question: Does the B49 registry hold also cover the i2s dispatch, and what does i2s need that i2r did not?
row_liveness.answer: Yes. The read hold is taken before the lookup (:271-273) and lives to the end of X509V3_EXT_print, so it covers the slot read (:323-332), the callback (:346) and the release (:374-381). No second hold was added. The i2s arm needs the row live through the callback, not merely through the slot read, because it passes `method` to the callback and enum_i2s reads `method->usr_data`; the existing hold supplies exactly that.
row_liveness.static_rows: The 11 callbacks are installed only in crate-owned `pub static` rows (or the helper-constructed `ossl_v3_ns_ia5_list`/`ossl_v3_utf8_list`), reached through STANDARD_EXTS; those rows are process-lifetime statics that X509V3_EXT_cleanup cannot release.
row_liveness.dynamic_rows: X509V3_EXT_add_alias copies a row (including i2s and usr_data) into a DYNAMIC allocation; X509V3_EXT_cleanup releases it through ext_list_free. The read hold keeps such an alias live for the whole print.
row_liveness.caller_rows: X509V3_EXT_add also accepts a caller-owned row and the list borrows it (only DYNAMIC rows are freed on cleanup). The registry lock protects the list, not the caller's storage: a caller that frees a registered row while a print uses it retains that obligation (B50-R1).

defect_class.existing: uncontracted unsafe fn definitions at 11 X509_VERIFY_POLICY i2s sites; the blocks had per-line SAFETY comments but no fn-level # Safety
defect_class.extension: none functional: the B49 dispatcher already holds the registry read lock across the i2s arm. The i2s-specific requirement is that the row stay live through the callback (enum_i2s reads method->usr_data), which the same hold provides.

hidden_obligations_note: The retained obligations are stated in the fn-level contracts and in B50-R1/R2/R3/R4: the registrar must keep each row's `it` and `usr_data` paired with its i2s, caller-registered row storage must outlive the list, the result must be one whole seam block with a NUL terminator, and the decoded value is exclusively the dispatcher's. Row liveness for DYNAMIC rows is enforced by the B49 read/write hold. None is hidden.
new_unsafe_assumptions_note: No production unsafe fn was added. The i2s arm reuses the B49 read hold and the existing decoder/item guards. The only new unsafe operation is the test-only recording_i2s callback.
test_only_unsafe_added_note: The test-only `unsafe extern "C" fn recording_i2s(...)` in src/x509/v3_prn.rs tests, used by the dispatcher-guard canary.
boundary_size: 11 boundary operations: the 11 i2s slot callbacks of registered extension rows, over 11 files. 11 V1 census sites retained; no new boundary rows for the 42 untouched sites.
safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: Kept true: all 11 sites remain reachable only as unsafe extern "C" callbacks through the unsafe X509V3_EXT_print entry point. The dispatcher refuses a NULL out/ext, a NULL item and a NULL decode before the slot. The remaining stated obligations are the registrar's row/usr_data pairing (B50-R2, B50-R4), the caller-registered row's lifetime (B50-R1) and the callback result's seam/NUL contract (B50-R3). No safe Rust path to these callbacks exists.

residuals.description: X509V3_EXT_add accepts a caller-owned row and the list borrows it (only X509V3_EXT_DYNAMIC rows are released by cleanup). The registry lock protects list mutation, not the caller's storage; a caller that frees a registered row while a print uses it retains that obligation. The authority has the same contract.

The dispatcher establishes that the value was decoded through the row's declared item, not that the item is the type the i2s body expects. A caller may register a row whose `it` and `i2s` disagree; the row pairing is the registrar's ABI obligation (carried from B49-R2).

A non-NULL i2s result must be one whole seam block and NUL-terminated within it; the dispatcher adopts it and prints it with `%s`, then frees it once. A callback that returns static, borrowed or unterminated storage violates the contract and can cause UB; this cannot be checked cheaply.
enum_i2s reads `method->usr_data` as a `BitStringBitname` array terminated by a NULL `lname`. The standard row pairs it with CRL_REASONS; a caller-registered row must make the same pairing.

An external caller that obtains a row through X509V3_EXT_get/_get_nid and then calls `method->i2s` outside X509V3_EXT_print gets no registry read hold: the ABI cannot carry the guard past the return. Such a caller must exclude a concurrent X509V3_EXT_cleanup itself.

If the registry lock cannot be created or acquired, X509V3_EXT_print answers 0 without running the callback; the authority has no lock and would proceed. Valid-call return values and printed bytes are unchanged.
A NULL out/ext, a NULL item accessor and a NULL decode are refused before the i2s slot; the authority would fault or pass NULL onward. These are the B49-R5/R6/R7 divergences, inherited unchanged.
The other 42 X509_VERIFY_POLICY sites remain BLOCKED: v2i 10, s2i 9, i2v 7, r2i 6, print 4, audit 2, bitst 2, non-method 2. No contract or guard is claimed for them.
No Miri (Stacked/Tree Borrows), ASan, TSan, dudect, authority differential or full library suite was run. Only the FAST gate and the focused x509:: tests were observed.
Only four of the 11 callbacks are driven end-to-end (group_ac, crl_reason, crl_number, subject_key_identifier); the other seven are covered by contract review and the shared dispatcher tests.
